question: Does the smallest cross-group pair have a global torsor obstruction despite passing the small-prime tests, compared with a soluble pair sharing one cover?
selection: Cross pair minimizes the maximum primitive quadratic coefficient height, then the minimum height and labels, among the 75 cross-group pairs in the frozen local-block input: orbit-11278 with orbit-1795d. Positive control fixes orbit-1795d and takes its least-coefficient-height partner in the observed +8 quartet: orbit-0911e. Selection is retrospective and predates this descent.
construction: Parametrize the common conic u^2=f_1795d(t) using its already recorded single-cover rational point. Substituting into the partner equation produces a binary quartic and a degree-two rational divisor, so the resulting genus-one torsor has period dividing two. Compute its Jacobian by quartic invariants and cross-check Sage's Jacobian constructor.
local_completion: Factor 2*disc(f)*disc(g)*Res(f,g), prove the factors prime, and provide exact Qp square-value witnesses at every prime in that support and a real witness. Outside this set the projective genus-one intersection has smooth reduction; the finite-field genus-one bound and Hensel imply a local point. Missing witnesses stay UNKNOWN.
descent: PARI ellrank effort zero on each auxiliary Jacobian. Its unconditional outputs give rank bounds and the CT quantity s; full Selmer dimension is upper_rank + rational_2_torsion_dimension + s. Matching rank bounds imply exact Sha[2] dimension s. If rank bounds match and s=0, everywhere-local solubility implies global solubility of the period-two carrier.
checkpoint: Immutable input, per-carrier geometry checkpoint, local checkpoint and descent checkpoint; keep timeout/failure outputs. No adaptive effort increase or new carrier selection on a failure.
boundary: Global nonemptiness of the parameter carrier is distinct from a lift above a prescribed specialization. No points on new original fibres are sought or forwarded. No rank bound for an original elliptic fibre is inferred from the auxiliary Jacobian rank.
